1.e4 d6 2.d4 g6.background: The same position arises from 1.e4 g6 2.d4 d6, the Modern Defence, also known as the Robatsch Defence. The tenth edition of Modern Chess Openings (1965) grouped the Pirc and the Robatsch together as the Pirc–Robatsch Defence.

1.e4 d6 2.d4 g6 3.Nc3.strategy: Develops and guards the e4 pawn, so White builds a broad pawn centre without hurry. Black's fianchettoed bishop will press on that centre from a distance, and White decides how to meet it: the game is a test of whether the centre is a strength or a target.

1.e4 d6 2.d4 g6 3.Nc3 c6.strategy: A waiting set-up: the pawn frees the queen's route to b6 and prepares queenside expansion, while the knight and bishop are left for later. The price is that White gets time to extend the centre before Black has challenged it.
1.e4 d6 2.d4 g6 3.Nc3 c6.name: Rat Defence: Accelerated Gurgenidze
